answers: Papillion Sophie has lived a pampered life, but that doesn't have to end now that her famous owner—Hollywood legend Lauren Bacall—has died. According to estate papers filed last week, Bacall left $10,000 to her son Sam Robards for Sophie's care and upkeep, Page Six reports. This bequeath isn't a surprise, considering Bacall called herself a "dog yearner" in a 2008 interview, Us reports. "I didn't have a dog growing up in the city with a working mother. As an only child, I yearned for someone to talk to," she said. She gave Sophie quite a glitzy life attending book signings and film festivals. Bacall didn't ignore her human family: The New York Daily News reports her $26.6 million estate was mostly split among her three children; her grandkids reportedly got $250,000 each. And two of her employees also received $20,000 and $15,000, respectively. Considering other famous four-legged heirs, Sophie's 10 grand isn't shocking: Leona Helmsley left $12 million to her Maltese and Alexander McQueen left $82,000 to his three dogs. But the oddest may be Dusty Springfield, who gave orders that her cat be serenaded with her own music and "marry" another cat.

full.prediction:
**Summary of News on Lauren Bacall's Estate and Legacy**

Lauren Bacall, the legendary actress who passed away at the age of 89 in August 2014, left behind a substantial estate valued at approximately $26.6 million. Her will, filed in Manhattan Surrogate’s Court, outlined the distribution of her wealth among her family, employees, and her beloved dog, Sophie, a Papillon.

Bacall, known for her iconic role in the film *To Have and Have Not* and her enduring romance with Humphrey Bogart, ensured that her son Sam Robards, who also acted, would be responsible for Sophie’s care. To support this, she left $10,000 to Robards. This gesture, while generous, was not unusual for celebrities who wish to provide for their pets. For instance, Leona Helmsley left $12 million to her Maltese dog, Trouble, and Alexander McQueen left $82,000 to his three dogs.

The majority of Bacall’s estate was divided among her three children: Leslie Bogart, Stephen Bogart, and Sam Robards. Each child received a share of the estate, which included her co-op apartment in the Dakota building on Central Park West, as well as her royalties and other personal property. In addition, Bacall left $250,000 to each of her six grandchildren, with the stipulation that the funds could be accessed when they turned 30.

Two of her long-time employees, Maria Santos and Ilsa Hernandez, were also named in her will. Santos received $20,000, while Hernandez, who had worked as her maid for 14 years, was surprised to learn she would receive $15,000. Bacall expressed gratitude for her employees’ service and dedication.

In her will, Bacall also requested that her children keep certain personal items, including letters, writings, and diaries, private. She named all three of her children as executors of her estate and emphasized her wish to be remembered not only for her first husband, Humphrey Bogart, but also for her second husband, Jason Robards, despite their eventual divorce.

Bacall’s legacy extends beyond her film career. She was a Tony Award winner, an honorary Oscar recipient, and a beloved figure in Hollywood. Her life was marked by a deep love for dogs, a passion for the arts, and a strong sense of personal
